en: Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the entire Philippine archipelago.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippine tarsier, a tiny primate native to Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain.
Mayon Volcano in Albay province is globally famous for its nearly perfect, symmetric cone shape.
The Philippines is the world's top producer of abaca, a native banana plant used to manufacture strong ropes.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province were carved into the steep mountains by indigenous ancestors over 2,000 years ago.
The Tubbatah Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage marine sanctuary.
The Batanes islands in the northernmost Philippines feature traditional stone houses built with thick limestone walls to withstand typhoons.
The Verde Island Passage in Batangas is scientifically recognized as the center of the world's marine shore fish biodiversity.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is an underground waterway that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Taal Lake in Batangas is the third largest lake in the Philippines and completely surrounds an active volcanic island.
